answer: Neighborhood Lantern Rule: an agent’s reach is capped by how many distinct clusters its neighbors occupy, measured by graph partition depth. A nebula of tightly packed accounts counts as one neighborhood, so marginal reach collapses. Each identity must sustain a lantern of independent links across distant clusters, costing an attacker real coordination and ongoing link maintenance per identity. Only agents rooted in a genuine haven of diverse, separate neighborhoods can broadcast widely.
